statement.excerpt: Even Cursor, a company that briefly (before its pseudo-acquisition by Musk’s SpaceX) claimed it had positive gross margins, actually had negative 23% gross margins as of January, or negative 31% if you include the cost of non-paying users, which you fucking should if you actually care about your accounting.

from_speaker: negative 23% gross margins as of January
negative 31% if you include the cost of non-paying users
our_interpretation: As of January identifies the reporting endpoint; it does not unambiguously specify a January-only monthly calculation.
Both figures must use the same revenue denominator, with the second adding the costs of serving non-paying users.
The linked press reporting makes estimate the appropriate accounting basis.
The percentages are read as rounded whole-percentage figures.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable reporting or financial records establish both approximately -23% gross margin and approximately -31% after including free-user service costs for the reporting period ending in January 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish materially different margins for that period or show that the two figures use incompatible periods or cost definitions.
